text:
incidents-bot: ALERT P1 · sudden p95 latency spike on /v1/generate (serving-runtime). Start: 2859004300. Error rate up ~15%, queue depth increasing on g4-pool-A. Routing impact: some customer requests queued >1s.

maya: paging oncall — I'm taking first pass. pulling traces + tail logs now.

rishi: I see large queue lengths on g4-pool-A and avg batch size jumped to ~48. No deploy in last hour.

samir: quick thought — this looks like a sudden fanout of many short requests causing large batches and long tail latency. Two levers: shrink max_batch + reduce batch_window_ms, and apply short-term rate shaping at gateway.

maya: agreed. planning to: 1) reduce max_batch for /v1/generate on g4-pool-A 64->16, 2) batch_window_ms 40->10ms, 3) apply temporary rate cap for anon keys RPS 50.

maya: executing now: `redwoodctl config update --pool g4-pool-A --route /v1/generate --max-batch 16 --batch-window-ms 10`

incidents-bot: CONFIG CHANGE queued -> applied (2859004360).

maya: also setting gateway limit: `redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope route --route /v1/generate --rps 50 --scope-key anonymous`

taylor: I'll also route lower-priority traffic to smaller quantized model to reduce pressure: `redwoodctl routing set --route /v1/generate --traffic-shape "tier:low->llama-13b-q"` — doing that now.

samir: good. will flip continuous-batching preemption on so small requests can be dispatched faster: `redwoodctl config patch --pool g4-pool-A --continuous-batching "preempt=true"`

maya: patch applied (2859004395). Observing metrics: queue depth dropping, p95 start going down from ~1.2s -> 420ms.

rishi: nice. support impact list: demo-shop and searchly experienced increased latency for ~3m each, some 429s for anonymous keys.

kate: I'm drafting customer note for demo-shop/searchly and posting to status page. Short message: "We observed elevated latency and rate-limited anonymous traffic; mitigation in progress; no data loss." Will tag customers.

support-bot: status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2859004321 · message sent to demo-shop/searchly via ticket #4521 #4522.

maya: p95 now ~280ms, error rate down to normal. Will keep reduced batch sizes + gateway cap for 15 minutes to ensure stability, then gradually relax.

samir: recommendation for rollback plan: after stable 15m -> increase max_batch to 32 and batch_window_ms to 20ms, monitor p95 and queue depth; if tail rises, revert immediately.

rishi: enabling short-term autoscaling burst for g4-pool-A to add 2 nodes as safety: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool g4-pool-A --delta +2 --ttl 10m` — done.

maya: handoff: I'm going off pager in 8m. handing to @rishi — summary: applied max_batch=16, batch_window_ms=10ms, continuous-batching preempt=true, anon RPS 50, routed low-tier to quantized model, scaled +2 nodes temporarily. Observed p95 drop -> stable.

rishi: taking handoff. I'll keep eyes on it, will relax gateway cap after 15m if stable.

kate: support note sent to customers, monitoring for followups.

taylor: left a comment in runbook: "adaptive short-term throttles + batch-window shrink worked for sudden short-request fanout; add to playbook."

samir: post-incident action: add synthetic workload that simulates many short 50-100 token requests to catch this before prod. Also add automated alert for avg-batch-size > 40 for >60s.

rishi: relaxing anon RPS cap to 100 in 5m if stable.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE · mitigations applied; severity reduced to P2. last_state_check 2859004525.

rishi: relaxing anon RPS -> 100 now (2859004528). observing p95 steady 300ms.

maya: thanks team. I'll open a short postmortem PR with timeline + config diffs.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED · mitigations effective, queues normalizing, autoscale TTL expired, follow-ups assigned. closed at 2859004530. :white_check_mark:
